title: Real vs ideal gases and kinetic molecular theory; Ideal gas equation and gas laws
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM06#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM06#t4 term and clue written for the game; AM06#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM06#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM04#N.6b, AM06#N.3, AM04#N.10b, AM06#N.5, AM04#N.12, AM06#N.7, AM04#N.14, AM04#N.15a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ideal gas
items.clue: Obeys PV = nRT exactly: particles of negligible volume with no attractions.

items.label: Elastic collision
items.clue: An impact between particles in which the total energy of motion is unchanged.

items.label: Kinetic molecular theory
items.clue: Model that treats a gas as particles in constant, random, straight-line motion.

items.label: Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution
items.clue: Graph of number of particles against energy or speed: a peak, then a long tail.

questions.stem: A rigid 2.50 L flask contains O₂(g) at a pressure of 1.20 atm and a temperature of 27 °C. What is the mass of O₂ in the flask?

A sealed, rigid steel container holds N₂(g) at 300 K. When the container is heated to 450 K, the pressure of the gas increases. Which statement gives correct particulate-level reasoning for the claim that heating the gas raises its pressure?

options.text: The molecules have a higher average speed, so they hit the walls more often and with more force.
The molecules expand as they are heated, so they take up more of the space in the container.
The molecules move farther apart as they are heated, so they press outward on the walls.
The molecules collide with one another more often, so these extra collisions add to the gas pressure.

questions.stem: A weather balloon holds 5.00 L of helium at 1.00 atm and 25 °C. It rises to where the pressure is 0.500 atm and the temperature is −23 °C. Assuming no gas escapes, what is its new volume?
questions.explanation: V₂ = 5.00 × (1.00/0.500) × (250.15/298.15) = 8.39 L. Expansion from the pressure drop wins over shrinkage from cooling.

questions.stem: A rigid container holds a mixture of He(g) and Ar(g) at 300 K. A student claims that the He atoms and the Ar atoms have the same average speed, because the two gases are at the same temperature. Which evaluation of the student's claim is best?

options.text: It is correct: the temperature of a sample measures the average speed of its particles, whatever the mass.
It is correct: the particles in a sample at one temperature all move at one speed, whatever their mass.
It is incorrect: the average speed of a particle is set by its mass, and does not depend on temperature.
It is incorrect: the two average kinetic energies are equal, and the He atoms have the higher average speed.

questions.stem: A rigid 2.50 L container holds a mixture of 0.200 mol of He(g) and 0.300 mol of Ne(g) at 127 °C. What is the partial pressure of Ne in the container?
A sample of N₂(g) in a rigid container is heated from 300 K to 600 K. Which statement correctly describes the change?

options.text: The peak of the Maxwell–Boltzmann curve gets taller, so the entropy of the gas decreases.
The Maxwell–Boltzmann curve gets lower and broader, so the entropy of the gas increases.
The curve keeps its shape and shifts right, as every molecule's energy doubles.
The curve gets broader, so more molecules have exactly the average energy.

questions.explanation: Energies spread over a wider range, so energy is more dispersed: entropy rises. The area under the curve stays the same.

questions.stem: A 2.70 g sample of Al(s) reacts completely with excess HCl(aq) according to the equation 2 Al(s) + 6 HCl(aq) → 2 AlCl₃(aq) + 3 H₂(g). What volume of H₂(g) is produced, measured at 25 °C and 1.00 atm?
A sealed aerosol can is left in a car on a sunny day. At 20 °C the gas inside is at 3.00 atm. The can warms to 70 °C; its volume stays constant. What happens to the pressure inside the can?

options.text: It rises to 3.5 times its starting value.
It stays the same, because the volume is fixed.
